description: Truy Tinh là đội ngũ đam mê khoa học, y học và khám phá vũ trụ. Chúng tôi phát triển ASTRA, một hệ thống hỗ trợ theo dõi và chăm sóc sức khỏe phi hành gia, hướng tới khả năng hoạt động độc lập khi mất liên lạc với Trái Đất. Đội tìm kiếm những thành viên sáng tạo, có kỹ năng lập trình, AI, thiết kế UI/UX, phân tích dữ liệu hoặc kiến thức y sinh. Chúng tôi đề cao tinh thần hợp tác, tư duy khoa học và quyết tâm biến ý tưởng thành sản phẩm thực tế.
summary: Mars, 2050. Everyone is an astronaut—aboard a spacecraft, inside a habitat, or crossing a planetary landscape in a rover. Wherever the mission takes them, their health travels with them. AETHERION makes astronaut health monitoring an ongoing journey of discovery and care. Our demo brings NASA astronaut history, understandable health indicators, symptom-aware clinical questions, locally available medical references, and a continuing care record into one experience. A new symptom prompts relevant questions about onset, progression, and warning signs; a directly reported serious sign points toward timely human help. GATHER → EVALUATE → ACT → RECHECK connects observations, decisions, and outcomes, helping the crew understand changes and communicate with its medical lead. We have made this first demo as complete and explorable as possible, giving the 2050 vision a tangible beginning today. The same approach could help remote communities on Earth take a more active role in their own care. AETHERION imagines one connected health journey across spacecraft, bases, rovers, and personal devices: wherever humans travel, caring for our health can become an endless, fascinating journey of discovery.
details:
2050 — EVERYONE IS AN ASTRONAUT

Imagine a mission in 2050. One explorer travels aboard a spacecraft, another works inside a lunar or Martian base, and another crosses the surface in a rover. Each carries a changing health story. AETHERION's dream is that caring for that story becomes a fascinating, continuous part of the journey, wherever the crew goes.

THE CHALLENGE, MADE PERSONAL

NASA's health-monitoring challenge asks astronauts to gather health indicators, evaluate their status, and act during space missions. AETHERION connects the measurements, medical references, questions, decisions, and follow-up into one crew-facing experience. It helps a person ask: What changed? What does it mean in context? What should I check next? What happened after I acted?

WHAT THE DEMO ALREADY BRINGS TOGETHER

The mobile experience opens with a guided Demo into NASA's historical Mercury–Atlas 7 (MA-7) archive. Its locally bundled Android data presents 4 event groups, 19 timepoints, 18 metrics, and 83 reported values. Crewmates can explore a genuine piece of astronaut health history even without an Earth connection.

The bilingual Health Guide explains pulse, blood pressure, breathing rate, temperature, oxygen saturation, ECG, sleep, radiation exposure, and complete blood count. Each topic pairs plain-language meaning with measurement tips and source links. The Library connects that approachable guide to a local medical knowledge collection: 118 structured NASA CliFF reference records are stored with source information and served by the onboard-style AETHERION server. It is a practical starting point for real medical reference access when the internet is far away.

Clinical symptom hooks make the experience responsive. The structured interview recognizes reported symptoms and chooses relevant questions about onset, progression, breathing at rest, active bleeding, sudden one-sided weakness, exposure, injury, and other context. A directly reported serious warning sign leads the crew toward qualified human assistance. The question path remains available through the local server, and optional AI can select among the allowed follow-up questions.

Care gives each concern continuity: GATHER → EVALUATE → ACT → RECHECK. A crewmate records a concern and symptoms, reviews the situation, confirms the action taken, records the outcome, and returns for the next check. Timestamped events, source details, units, and data states help turn scattered numbers into a story the crew can revisit and discuss.

The AI workspace can use a locally configured Ollama model or an administrator-configured Gemini/OpenAI provider. The mobile client, local server, SQLite records, and separate native Qt desktop companion form one architecture for exploration, monitoring, and follow-up.

WHY THIS MATTERS

AETHERION places each crewmate at the center of their health journey. Authentic NASA history, approachable medical references, symptom-aware questions, and a continuing care record help them learn, notice changes earlier, and communicate clearly with their medical lead. We have brought the hackathon demo as close as possible to a complete, connected experience that people can explore today. The same idea can one day help remote communities on Earth take an active role in their own care when distance makes support harder to reach.

HOW WE BUILT IT

The mobile client uses Expo SDK 54, React Native, TypeScript, and JavaScript. The local server uses Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, and SQLite; the independent desktop companion uses Python, PySide6/Qt, and PyQtGraph. NASA MA-7, NASA's Integrated Medical Model CliFF documentation, OSDR, and the Human Research Program inform the scientific content. MedlinePlus contributes health education references. Codex and Gemini/Antigravity assisted research, code, debugging, design, and writing. Development used a standard Windows PC and an Android-class mobile target.

THE JOURNEY AHEAD

Today, AETHERION lets a crewmate explore a measurement, follow a symptom trail, consult medical knowledge, and return to the record after taking action. Our 2050 vision carries that same health journey from spacecraft to base to rover, across the personal devices and crew stations that accompany each explorer. Wherever humans travel, caring for our health can become an endless, fascinating journey of discovery.
